name: Trotskyism
summary: Trotskyism is the family of Marxist currents descended from Leon Trotsky's Left Opposition and the Fourth International. Its branches share socialist revolution led by a workers' party, rule by elected workers' councils, expropriation and democratic planning of the key economy, internationalism against imperialism and nationalism, and rejection of Stalinism. They differ on the nature of the USSR and on unions, identity politics and other questions.
scope: Family entry: answers only what independent Trotskyist currents share. Branches read from their own programmes: the ICFI/SEP (orthodox, Statement of Principles), the USFI (Mandel, 1985 resolution), the Cliffite IST (ISO Where We Stand, Cliff), the Militant/CWI tradition (Socialist Party), Morenism (LIT history) and Cannon's SWP. Trotsky's 1930s writings are the common origin, not counted as a branch. Lambertism was sought but no programme text could be opened, so it is not used. Orthodox-trotskyism, shachtmanism and posadism have their own entries. Positions held by one branch only are null; opposed positions are 0, low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The British Socialist Party programme demands a free, publicly run NHS, the SEP programme demands unrestricted access to quality medical care, and the USFI resolution lists a secure existence and social rights among workers' democracy's tasks.
